# ddot.it

> ddot.it is a minimal, plain-text triple syntax for building a personal or enterprise knowledge graph across any tool or document type. It is token-efficient, Markdown-compatible, and easy to type on any keyboard.

ddot.it lets you embed typed links (triples) directly in any text — source code comments, Markdown, YAML, AsciiDoc, plain text, and more. A **ddot collector** reads those sources, extracts all triples, and combines them into a single knowledge graph in Connected JSON (CJ) format.

For writing ddot.it, just read write.md and skip the rest.

## Syntax by Example

Every example below is a case from the golden corpus (`test-data/cases/`), named at the end of
its section. Input and output there are verified against the reference implementation, so these
are contracts, not illustrations.

**Reading the events.** Each recognised triple emits one JSON object. Every event also carries
`kind`, `source` and `location`, which are omitted below to keep the examples readable — see
"Output: Triple Events".

### A triple

```
Project Eagle ..started in.. 2024
```
```json
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"started in","to":"2024"}
```

Fields may contain spaces; only the operators delimit them. Leading and trailing whitespace is
stripped, so `Dirk   .. works at ..  SAP` gives the same three values as `Dirk ..works at.. SAP`.
`(01-simple-triple)`

### Untyped link — `....`

Use `....` (or `.. ..`) when the relation is just "see this". Both spellings are the same
operator and both mean the relation `links to`, which is **written out** in the event.

```
Project Eagle .... Moonshot
Alpha .. .. Beta
```
```json
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"links to","to":"Moonshot"}
{"from":"Alpha","type":"links to","to":"Beta"}
```
`(02-untyped-link, 10-spaced-untyped)`

### More facts about the same subject

Omit the subject and the previous line's subject continues. This works for the untyped form too.

```
Project Eagle ..started in.. 2024
..doc site.. example.com/docbase/8dcjsid
.... Moonshot
```
```json
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"started in","to":"2024"}
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"doc site","to":"example.com/docbase/8dcjsid"}
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"links to","to":"Moonshot"}
```

There is no shorthand for several objects of the same subject+relation — repeat the line.
`(07-leading-separator-continuation, 26-untyped-continuation)`

### Metadata: one pair

`,,` attaches metadata to the triple on its left.

```
John Doe ..leads.. Project Eagle ,, ..since.. 2025
```
```json
{"from":"John Doe","type":"leads","to":"Project Eagle","meta":[{"type":"since","to":"2025"}]}
```
`(03-inline-meta)`

### Metadata: a free-text note

Metadata does not have to be a pair. Plain text after `,,` is a **note**, and it carries the
built-in relation `text` — **not** `links to`.

```
John Doe ..leads.. Project Eagle ,, a random note
```
```json
{"from":"John Doe","type":"leads","to":"Project Eagle","meta":[{"type":"text","to":"a random note"}]}
```

The untyped `,, .... 2025` form is the one that means `links to`:

```
John Doe ..leads.. Project Eagle ,, .... 2025
```
```json
{"from":"John Doe","type":"leads","to":"Project Eagle","meta":[{"type":"links to","to":"2025"}]}
```
`(13-inline-meta-text, 24-untyped-inline-meta)`

### Metadata: several entries on one line, separated by `;;`

`;;` separates metadata **entries**. Pairs and notes mix freely, in any order, and the event
keeps the written order.

```
John Doe ..leads.. Project Eagle ,, ..since.. 2025 ;; ..until.. 2027
```
```json
{"from":"John Doe","type":"leads","to":"Project Eagle","meta":[{"type":"since","to":"2025"},{"type":"until","to":"2027"}]}
```

```
Dirk ..works at.. SAP ,, ..since.. 2016 ;; a random note ;; .... Walldorf ;; ..until.. 2020
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"since","to":"2016"},{"type":"text","to":"a random note"},{"type":"links to","to":"Walldorf"},{"type":"until","to":"2020"}]}
```

`;;` separates **unconditionally** — it ends a note exactly as it ends a pair's object:

```
Dirk ..works at.. SAP ,, first note ;; second note ;; third note
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"text","to":"first note"},{"type":"text","to":"second note"},{"type":"text","to":"third note"}]}
```

So a note containing a literal `;;` cannot be written inline — use the block form below.
`(22-inline-meta-separator, 37-inline-meta-mixed, 36-inline-meta-notes)`

### Metadata: block form

End the triple line with `,,`, put one entry per line, and close with `,,` on its own line.
Newlines separate the entries here, so `;;` is ordinary text inside a block.

```
Dirk Hagemann ..works at.. SAP ,,
..year.. 2010
..fictive.. yes
,,
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk Hagemann","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"year","to":"2010"},{"type":"fictive","to":"yes"}]}
```

Pairs and notes mix in a block too, in written order:

```
Dirk ..works at.. SAP ,,
..since.. 2016
a note between pairs
.... Walldorf
..until.. 2020
,,
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"since","to":"2016"},{"type":"text","to":"a note between pairs"},{"type":"links to","to":"Walldorf"},{"type":"until","to":"2020"}]}
```
`(04-multiline-meta, 39-block-meta-mixed)`

### Metadata: notes in a block fold together

**Adjacent** text lines are ONE note joined by newlines — which is what keeps a pasted paragraph
intact. A pair line ends the run; the next text line starts a new note.

```
Dirk ..works at.. SAP ,,
first note
still the first note
..since.. 2016
second note
,,
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"text","to":"first note\nstill the first note"},{"type":"since","to":"2016"},{"type":"text","to":"second note"}]}
```

Two *adjacent* notes are therefore not writable in a block. Use the inline `;;` form for that.
`(27-multiline-meta-text-lines, 38-block-meta-notes)`

### Metadata: less common block forms

The opening `,,` may stand alone on the line after the triple:

```
Project Eagle ..started in.. 2024
,,
free-form note line
,,
```
```json
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"started in","to":"2024","meta":[{"type":"text","to":"free-form note line"}]}
```

A block may be empty — the triple is still emitted, with no `meta` key at all:

```
Project Eagle ..started in.. 2024 ,,
,,
```
```json
{"from":"Project Eagle","type":"started in","to":"2024"}
```

`;;` inside a block is content, not a separator:

```
Dirk Hagemann ..works at.. SAP ,,
..note.. first ;; second
,,
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk Hagemann","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"note","to":"first ;; second"}]}
```
`(09-standalone-comma-block, 25-empty-meta-block, 28-semicolon-in-meta-block)`

### `!!this` — annotate the document itself

```
ddot.it/this ..project.. Code Red
!!this ..author.. Alice
```
```json
{"from":"ddot.it/this","type":"project","to":"Code Red"}
{"from":"!!this","type":"author","to":"Alice"}
```

The parser emits the command verbatim; the collector substitutes the document's source URI.
`(16-this, 05-command, 11-shorthand-command)`

### `!!off` / `!!on` — exclude a region

Recognised **anywhere on a line**, including inside a host language's own comment syntax.
Nothing between them is parsed.

```
Active ..likes.. Coffee
<!-- ddot.it/off -->
Draft ..maybe.. ship it
# !!on
Back ..works.. now
```
```json
{"from":"Active","type":"likes","to":"Coffee"}
{"from":"Back","type":"works","to":"now"}
```

Caution: this also fires in prose *about* the commands — writing "use `!!off`" really does turn
parsing off.
`(06-off-on-toggle, 31-off-in-comment)`

### `!!block` — a multi-line, verbatim value

The value becomes the lines from the next line down to the terminator: the first **blank line**,
or a custom `?end=MARKER`. Nothing inside is interpreted, so `..`, `,,` and commands stay literal.

```
john ..address.. ddot.it/block
Broadway 1
Berlin
Germany

john ..age.. 11
```
```json
{"from":"john","type":"address","to":"Broadway 1\nBerlin\nGermany"}
{"from":"john","type":"age","to":"11"}
```

With `?end=`, blank lines no longer terminate — which is the reason to use it:

```
john ..address.. !!block?end=END
1 Broad Way
Lower Manhatten

U.S.A.
END
Dirk ..works at.. SAP
```
```json
{"from":"john","type":"address","to":"1 Broad Way\nLower Manhatten\n\nU.S.A."}
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP"}
```
`(17-block, 21-block-end-marker)`

### `!!block` in the other three positions

`!!block` opens only when it **fills a whole field and ends its line**, and only in four
positions: subject, object, meta-object, and meta text. After the terminator the logical line
resumes, so one triple can carry several blocks.

Subject (the only way to write a subject containing `..`):

```
!!block
Alice
Anderson

..knows.. Bob
```
```json
{"from":"Alice\nAnderson","type":"knows","to":"Bob"}
```

Meta object, then a `;;` continuation after the terminator:

```
Dirk ..works at.. SAP ,, ..note.. !!block
line one

;; ..until.. 2020
```
```json
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP","meta":[{"type":"note","to":"line one"},{"type":"until","to":"2020"}]}
```

Meta text (allowed but redundant — the `,,` … `,,` block says the same thing):

```
water ..formula.. H2O ,, !!block
solid, liquid, gas -- all three
phases occur naturally

Dirk ..works at.. SAP
```
```json
{"from":"water","type":"formula","to":"H2O","meta":[{"type":"text","to":"solid, liquid, gas -- all three\nphases occur naturally"}]}
{"from":"Dirk","type":"works at","to":"SAP"}
```

A `!!block` in a relation or meta-relation, or in the middle of running text, is inert.
`(29-block-subject, 33-meta-block-continuation, 34-block-meta-text, 32-chained-blocks)`

### What is NOT a triple

Symbol characters (`.`, `,`, `;`, `!`) form **maximal runs**, and a run is an operator only at
its exact length. One dot, three dots, five dots, a lone comma — all ordinary text. A line that
is not a triple emits **nothing**; it is not an error.

```
Just some ordinary prose here.
Wait... what did you say?
A lone .. in prose, only one marker.
Mr. Smith went to U.S.A. today.
Node.js and j-s-o-n.org are fine.
See https://example.com/a?b=1 for details.
```

Six lines in, zero events out.

By the same rule an **object** may contain `..`, because it is bounded by `,,` and not by dots:

```
a ..spec.. http://h/x..y
a ..links to.. ../../b.adoc
j-s-o-n.org ..has type.. project
```
```json
{"from":"a","type":"spec","to":"http://h/x..y"}
{"from":"a","type":"links to","to":"../../b.adoc"}
{"from":"j-s-o-n.org","type":"has type","to":"project"}
```

Values are emitted **verbatim** — no unescaping, no HTML escaping, no quote stripping:

```
Repo ..hosts.. <https://example.com/x?a=1&b=2>
ddot.it/this ..is.. "a sample document"
```
```json
{"from":"Repo","type":"hosts","to":"<https://example.com/x?a=1&b=2>"}
{"from":"ddot.it/this","type":"is","to":"\"a sample document\""}
```
`(23-not-a-triple, 20-object-dotdot, 12-dotted-subject, 08-html-escaping, 05-command)`

### Whitespace and line endings

Newline normalisation happens before parsing: `CR LF` → NL, `LF` → NL, `CR` → NL. Whitespace
(`WS`) is TAB plus every Unicode space separator (category `Zs`) — so NBSP (U+00A0) and NARROW
NO-BREAK SPACE (U+202F) count as whitespace, because they are visually indistinguishable from a
space and would otherwise create a different node that looks identical. Zero-width characters
(U+200B, U+FEFF) are category `Cf` and are ordinary text. `(35-unicode-whitespace)`

### Formal grammar

The grammar is **not** repeated here. It lives in
`site/spec/ddot.it-parsing.ebnf` — EBNF in the notation of
[XML 1.0, section 6](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-notation), with `|` read as ordered choice
and `?`/`*`/`+` as greedy. It is included verbatim in the Parse Specification
(`site/spec/ddot-it-parse.adoc`, rendered at /spec/ddot-it-parse.html#grammar), which is the
normative definition and also carries the token alphabet, the parse state automaton, and the AST.

In case of doubt the golden corpus at `test-data/cases/` has the last word.

## Standard Relation Types

| Name          | Aliases                | Semantics                                                                 |
|---------------|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `related`     | `rel`, `is related`    | Undirected link between A and B                                           |
| `same as`     | `is same as`           | A and B refer to the same concept                                         |
| `is alias of` |                        | Like `same as` but with a clear main concept (symlink semantics)          |
| `links to`    | `link`, `see also`     | Directed untyped link; default when `....` is used                        |
| `has tag`     | `tag`                  | A has tag B; not transitive                                               |
| `has type`    | `type`, `is a`         | A has type B (like rdf:type); inherited via `has subtype`                 |
| `has subtype` | `subtype`              | Transitive specialisation; cycles imply `same as`                         |
| `text`        |                        | A free-text note attached as metadata (see the examples above)            |

## Commands

Commands are URLs starting with `ddot.it/` (or abbreviated with `!!`). The **slash and a name are
required**; `?` and `#` do not terminate a command but introduce its query and fragment, so
`!!block?end=EOS` is a single command. A command is part of the text of the field holding it.
All four spellings are interpreted identically: `https://ddot.it/NAME`, `http://ddot.it/NAME`,
`ddot.it/NAME`, `!!NAME`.

- `ddot.it` — a document *marker*, not a command. It hints that the file contains ddot.it syntax.
  Readers scan **every** file by default, so the marker only selects files in the optional
  "exclude non-marked files" mode.
- `ddot.it/this` — refers to the current document as the triple subject
- `ddot.it/on` — start processing this region (include)
- `ddot.it/off` — stop processing this region (exclude)
- `ddot.it/block` — the rest of the value is taken verbatim from the following lines,
  up to a blank line or a custom `?end=MARKER`. Allowed in the subject, object,
  metadata-object and metadata-text positions, and only when it ends its line.

The parser recognises command **syntax** without any registry of names, so an unknown or retired
name is still a command token; deciding what it *means* is the interpreting layer's job.

## Output: Triple Events

Each recognized triple fires one JSON event:
```json
{ "from": "Project Eagle", "type": "started in", "to": "2024",
  "kind": "markdown", "source": "/README.md", "location": 1 }
```

Fields, in this fixed key order:

- `from` — the subject. An omitted subject is already substituted here.
- `type` — the relation. **Always present, never omitted**: an untyped `....` link carries the
  literal string `links to`, and a free-text note carries `text`. A consumer never has to default
  a missing field.
- `to` — the object. Never empty.
- `meta` — array of `{type, to}`, the same two keys as the triple, in source order. **Omitted**
  when the triple has none — never an empty array.
- `kind` — the host format the reader read (`ddot`, `markdown`, `asciidoc`, `java`, …).
- `source` — the chunk's source URI. This is what `!!this` stands for.
- `location` — 1-based line number of the triple's first line.

Values are emitted verbatim. Serialisation is JSON Lines: one event per line, UTF-8, no enclosing
array. A line that is not a triple emits nothing.

The normative definition is the Parse Specification, section "Triple Events"
(`site/spec/ddot-it-parse.adoc`, rendered at /spec/ddot-it-parse.html#events).

## Knowledge Graph Data Model

Triples are stored as a tree: **entity → type → value → entries**. Each entry holds source location (`kind`, `url`, `line`) and optional metadata. Duplicate triples produce multiple entries for the same (entity, type, value) key.

Output is in [Connected JSON](https://j-s-o-n.org) (CJ) format, convertible to other graph formats at [GraphInOut.com](https://graphinout.com).

## Documentation

- [User Guide](https://ddot.it/user-guide.html): Full syntax reference, commands, and standard relation types
- [Developer Guide](https://ddot.it/developer-guide.html): Architecture, formal syntax grammar, triple event spec, collector spec

## Reader Specs

- [Markdown Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-markdown.html): Plain text, HTML comments, code blocks, section attributes
- [AsciiDoc Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-asciidoc.html): Line/block comments, listing blocks, block attributes
- [XML Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-xml.html): XML comments, element text; pom.xml patterns
- [YAML Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-yaml.html): Comments, string values; docker-compose patterns
- [Java Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-java.html): Line comments, block comments, Javadoc, `@DdotIt` annotation
- [Plain Text Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-plaintext.html): Any line of plain text
- [HTML Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-html.html): HTML comments, element text, `data-ddot` attributes
- [PowerPoint Reader](https://ddot.it/reader-powerpoint.html): Slide text, speaker notes

## Optional

- [GraphInOut.com](https://graphinout.com): Convert Connected JSON to other graph formats (RDF, GraphML, etc.)
- [j-s-o-n.org](https://j-s-o-n.org): Connected JSON format specification
